title: Hybrid sketch telemetry fabric for per-tenant percentile extrapolation and trace-linked KPIs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current metric ingestion pipeline suffers from cardinality explosion and inaccurate tail-percentile estimates for low-volume tenants and infrequently used model routes. Additionally, linking aggregated per-request KPIs (latency, error) back to traces is brittle when sampling and label-scrubbing happen downstream.

Proposal: Implement a Hybrid Sketch Telemetry Fabric component sitting in the ingestion tier (sidecar/edge and central aggregator). It will: 1) compute streaming sketches (DDSketch primary, HDR optional) for latency and token-count distributions on a per-tenant, per-model, per-route basis; 2) use deterministic reservoir/reservoir+hash sampling for creating lightweight exemplar sets that preserve high-value outliers and enable trace linkage; 3) emit both Prometheus-compatible rolling-quantile metrics and OTLP metric envelopes with exemplar references to span IDs; 4) perform fingerprint enrichment (model_version, route_hash, request_type) with privacy-safe truncation rules; 5) adapt sketch granularity by tenant-tier and traffic volume to bound memory.

Outcome: More accurate SLO-aligned percentiles (P50/P95/P99) across tenant scales, stable cardinality budgets, and robust metric->trace root-cause where exemplars exist.
acceptance_criteria: Deployed sketching sidecar runs on a subset of inference nodes and produces DDSketch-based P50/P95/P99 estimates within 3% of ground-truth for high-traffic routes and within 10% for low-traffic routes compared to full aggregation (benchmark harness)
Exemplar reservoir contains trace/span_id references for at least 99% of top-1% latency samples during test window and those references can be resolved by the tracing backend to meaningful spans
Prometheus-compatible endpoints expose summary-style quantiles and exemplar links; Prometheus scrape tests succeed with <1s extra scrape time per target in staging
OTLP exporter emits metric points with exemplar attributes and an attestable fingerprint label set, consumed by the central metric router without schema errors
Memory footprint per sidecar < 200MB at 95th percentile for standard tenants and makes graceful trade-off decisions (coarsen buckets) for extreme cardinality tenants
Migration can be rolled out with canary targeting 5% of traffic and rollback completes within 10 minutes if errors exceed thresholds
Docs/Console: Dashboard cards exist showing sketch-derived P95/P99 and exemplar-linked traces; runbooks updated for SLO alerting using sketch-derived metrics
notes: Design choices considered: DDSketch chosen for relative-error bounded quantiles; HDR provides fixed-bucket guarantees but higher memory for long tails
Fingerprinting policy: keep model_id and hashed model_version truncated to 8 chars; route names truncated and normalized to reduce cardinality while enabling rollup queries
Privacy/compliance: hashed values are salted per-tenant; retention of exemplar span IDs adheres to data-retention policy and can be disabled per tenant
Fallback path: if exemplar resolution fails, metric points still emitted and central router tags them with resolution_status=unresolved so dashboards can degrade gracefully
We need a short RFC for gateway-to-central protocol additions: exemplar attribute format and OTLP semantic conventions extension
Trade-offs: tighter memory caps increase quantile error; aggressive fingerprint truncation reduces ability to debug complex multi-model flows
implementation_steps: Prototype DDSketch sidecar in Rust with a gRPC control API and minimal config flags (bucket sizing, reservoir_size, fingerprinting policy)
Benchmarks: run against replayed production request traces (Jan-Feb 2026) to verify accuracy and memory characteristics
Extend our OTLP ingestion schema (patch to central router) to accept exemplar references and fingerprint labels
Instrument a small canary fleet (5% of dedicated inference pool) with sidecars and add dashboards for comparison vs existing rollups
Add Prometheus scrape compatibility layer (summary/exemplar endpoints) and test Prometheus federation in staging
Implement admin config for tenant-tier policies and per-tenant disable switch for exemplars due to privacy/customer requests
Code reviews, security review, and perf signoff; then gradual ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%
Post-mortem and lessons learned after full rollout; consider expanding HDR option for specific high-cardinality tenants
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected memory blow-ups for tenants with many model_version combinations; Mitigation: circuit-breaker to coarsen buckets and emit a metric that signals fallback
Risk: Overlinking traces may leak PII via exemplar attributes; Mitigation: strict sanitizer + opt-out + per-tenant salt
Risk: Central OTLP router schema changes break downstream consumers; Mitigation: dual-write mode (old envelope + new exemplar-enabled envelope) and feature flag
Risk: Prometheus scrape overhead increases; Mitigation: sample rate throttling and aggregation proxies for large scrape fanout
